semantics: Applicability is conjunctive over capabilities and requires_profiles, as in the binding corpus. Load the named message from fixture_file, deep-copy it, then apply each replace entry as an RFC 6901 pointer replacement before delivery. A replacement never adds a missing member. deliver_http is an authorized, current canonical HTTP 200 representation whose freshness and Age were validated; deliver_stream is a stream frame and never improves freshness. repair_result and canonical_poll_result are canonical HTTP responses with the generations named by the action. Expected projection descriptors omitted after installation are preserved exactly. Counts are cumulative observability counters. All time advances use a monotonic clock.

vectors.description: An authorized bootstrap snapshot installs atomically and becomes fresh.
A JSON Patch applies only over its exact base and advances to its target.
A Merge Patch independently requires the exact base and advances atomically.
Re-delivery of a non-idempotent patch is discarded by cursor and token.
A duplicate cannot extend freshness or stale lifetime.
The same semantic tuple from a stream is a non-refreshing duplicate, while a current canonical HTTP 200 revalidates it.
An authorized 304 with complete matching semantic headers is a revalidation, not a duplicate.
A 304 for the installed cursor and ETag with a mismatched state token is equivocation, cannot extend freshness, and closes the source.
A 304 for the installed cursor, token, and ETag with a mismatched state digest is equivocation and cannot renew freshness.
An older snapshot cannot roll back a newer installed version.
A patch whose base is ahead of local state is not applied and starts one repair.
A syntactically valid patch that cannot apply leaves the previous state untouched.
A snapshot whose recomputed JCS digest differs from target is never installed.
A schema-valid but semantically wrong patch result is rejected by its recomputed digest and repaired by snapshot.
A patch path capable of prototype pollution is rejected before application.
Two representations for the same cursor are producer equivocation, and a later in-band snapshot cannot clear the fatal generation.
A second representation with the same cursor and state token but different state and digest is producer equivocation.
The same CloudEvents source/id with different JCS content is an identity collision, never an early duplicate discard.
A frame for an installed stream id from a different CloudEvents source is rejected atomically and quarantines the source.
A frame whose subject no longer names its installed stream id is rejected atomically and quarantines the source.
A frame that reuses an installed stream id for another projection is rejected atomically without replacing the fixed tuple.
A frame that reuses an installed stream id for another partition is rejected atomically without replacing the fixed tuple.
A frame cannot reclassify an installed public stream as tenant data; it is rejected atomically and the source is quarantined.
An event from another epoch triggers repair; only its authoritative repair snapshot resets state.
A repair callback from an older local generation cannot reinstall the epoch replaced by a newer repair.
A patch cannot cross projection schema versions.
Repeated invalidations retain usable data and coalesce into one repair at the newest head.
An unknown invalidation at the exact installed head cannot be dismissed as data_changed and forces canonical validation.
An invalidation head older than the installed state cannot make current data stale.
An invalidation that contradicts the installed token at the same cursor is equivocation.
A gap whose head is behind the installed state is a regression and cannot reset it.
SSE may enter backoff while an HTTP repair remains active and usable data stays installed.
A retention gap discards incremental buffers and requests a full snapshot without erasing usable data early.
Queue overflow becomes reset and full repair rather than unbounded buffering.
Freshness and stale-if-error expire on monotonic elapsed time.
A principal change purges protected state regardless of freshness.
A callback captured under the previous principal cannot install after a security-generation change.
A higher semantic sequence is accepted even when its CloudEvents time is earlier.
Out-of-order delivery starts repair and converges to the authoritative head snapshot.
Without a durable outbox, canonical polling repairs an update for which no stream event existed.

actions.note: Exceeds max_canonical_reconcile_interval_ms plus its jitter bound.

vectors.description: Accepted records durability of the command request but not completion of its effect.
Retrying the same command id and fingerprint replays one durable result.
vectors.notes: The projection is still absent locally; a receipt fence does not install projection state.

vectors.description: Reusing a command id for a different intention returns conflict and does not execute again.
A lost response becomes unknown until receipt lookup; SSE observation is not used as proof.
A terminal receipt may arrive first; a later accepted revision is discarded as regression.
A different terminal status after commit is producer equivocation for that command.
The same receipt revision cannot carry a different token or result.
A higher receipt revision may add observation fences without changing its terminal result.

A higher authorized receipt revision may replace a same-stream observation fence after a legitimate epoch change, an out-of-order older revision cannot undo it, and a later reuse of the abandoned epoch is invalid.
A later receipt revision cannot move the immutable retry horizon.
The server recomputes the fingerprint and rejects a changed body even when the client repeats the old digest.
Retry after the monotonic retry horizon returns 410, remains locally unknown, and never creates a second effect.
A patch with matching cursor/token but the wrong base digest is not an exact base and cannot apply.
After invalidate head 20, gap head 20/floor 15 still resets a client whose installed base is 10.
An accepted command reaches an explicit terminal indeterminate receipt and cannot be retried automatically.
Rejected revision 3 followed by committed revision 2 is the same terminal conflict as the opposite arrival order.
Accepted revision 3 followed by terminal revision 2 is invalid instead of remaining accepted.
Terminal revision 2 followed by accepted revision 3 reaches the same absorbing invalid state.
A pending command from the old principal is not retried under the new security generation.
Installing a passive update does not steal focus or overwrite an unrelated local draft.
